items.stem: How should tables be designed in Cassandra?

options.text: Around the queries the application will run
options.rationale: Correct: Cassandra uses query-driven modeling, shaping tables to serve specific queries.

options.text: Fully normalized like a relational schema
options.rationale: Full normalization forces joins that Cassandra does not do efficiently.
Cassandra does not support arbitrary joins.

options.text: With one table for the entire database
options.rationale: A single table cannot serve diverse query patterns well.

items.explanation: Correct: Cassandra uses query-driven modeling, shaping tables to serve specific queries.

items.stem: What determines which node is responsible for a given row in Cassandra?

options.text: The token derived from the partition key
options.rationale: Correct: the partition key is hashed to a token that maps to a node on the ring.
Clustering columns order rows within a partition, not node placement.
Insertion order does not decide node ownership.
A secondary index does not determine partition placement.

items.explanation: Correct: the partition key is hashed to a token that maps to a node on the ring.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about consistency in Cassandra are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Read and write consistency levels together affect whether reads see the latest write
options.rationale: Correct: tuning both read and write levels (e.g. so they overlap) governs read-your-write behavior.

options.text: QUORUM requires a majority of replicas to respond
options.rationale: Correct: QUORUM needs a majority of replicas to acknowledge.

options.text: Cassandra offers only a single fixed consistency level
options.rationale: Cassandra offers tunable consistency per operation, not one fixed level.

options.text: Consistency level has no effect on availability trade-offs
options.rationale: Higher consistency reduces availability under failures; it is a trade-off.

items.explanation: Correct: tuning both read and write levels (e.g. so they overlap) governs read-your-write behavior.; Correct: QUORUM needs a majority of replicas to acknowledge.
